newsitem.title: USA: Global PC shipments up 16.3 pct in Q3 - Dataquest.
newsitem.headline: Global PC shipments up 16.3 pct in Q3 - Dataquest.

text.p: Shipments of personal computers worldwide rose 16.3 percent in the third quarter from a year earlier, market research firm Dataquest said.

Toshiba Corp nearly doubled its shipments and posted the fastest growth among top PC vendors, Dataquest said. Apple Computer Inc lost substantial ground, while preliminary third-quarter data showed Compaq Computer Corp remained the world's dominant PC supplier and International Business Machines Corp was second.
Dataquest said the PC market was on track to grow 19.7 percent in 1996 after record 24.7 percent growth in 1995.

Toshiba rocketed into the standings on shipments that soared 94.6 percent from a year earlier, making it the world's fifth largest PC supplier. One of the study's authors called this a remarkable acheivement because Toshiba mainly sells portable computers but relatively few desktop PCs.

"Given that portable computers account for less than 20 percent of the PC market, it's astounding that Toshiba could capture the No. 5 spot in the worldwide PC market," said Kimball Brown, a Dataquest PC analyst.
Compaq's share of the world PC market in the 1996 third quarter rose to 10.3 percent from 10.0 percent in the similar quarter a year ago, the Dataquest survey found.
IBM continued to gain ground during the third period, with shipments up 27.4 percent from a year ago, boosting IBM's market share to 8.6 percent from 7.9 percent a year earlier.

Apple Computer continued to show negative growth, as shipments slid 27.5 percent worldwide during the third quarter, causing its market share to decline to 5.4 percent from 8.7 percent a year ago, when it was the world's number two supplier and well ahead of IBM in shipments, it said.
Apple and Packard Bell Inc showed the largest declines among U.S. PC vendors, with shipments down 37.6 percent and 26.2 percent, respectively.
Compaq retained its top position in the U.S. PC market, while IBM leapfrogged over Packard Bell Inc to land in the number two U.S. spot.

Compaq's third-quarter U.S. shipments rose 33.4 percent from a year earlier, boosting its U.S. market share to 14.4 percent from 12.2 percent. Over the same period, IBM's U.S. shipments rose 24.1 percent, boosting its share of the U.S. market to 9.1 percent from 8.8 percent.
Packard Bell's U.S. market share fell to 7.8 percent from 11.9 percent a year ago.

Despite Packard Bell's decline, its combination with NEC Corp the world's fourth-largest supplier and Zenith Data Systems, make that group the second largest supplier in the U.S. PC market, Dataquest noted.

Dell Computer Corp shot into the top five rankings among U.S. PC suppliers by growing 85.2 percent year-to-year. It had 7.3 percent of the U.S. market in the third quarter, up from 4.4 percent a year ago.
"It appears that IBM's consumer offerings are catching Packard Bell in their strongest market," said Bill Schaub, director of Dataquest's worldwide tracking programs.
Schaub said one bright note for Apple was that its recently-announced price cuts could boost the overall number of PCs shipped during the upcoming fourth quarter.

Dataquest's study is based on preliminary shipping figures from more than 30 PC makers and is published quarterly. Reflecting the degree of fragmentation in the industry, the top five PC vendors amounted to only 33 percent of the total world market and 46 percent of the U.S. market.
